clues.RING: Band of color around the raccoon's tail
clues.WATER: Liquid flowing in the creek beside the raccoon
clues.TAIL: Ringed part extending behind a raccoon

notes.WATER: The water in the creek follows its channel. The bank is the ground at either side where the raccoon can walk.
notes.NIGHT: Raccoons often become active after dark. At night a raccoon can move along the creek bank looking for food.
notes.TAIL: A raccoon's tail shows dark rings around it. Those rings can help identify the animal even when its masked face is turned away.

small-wild-visitors-4.solvingTip: Find the face part you use to notice a smell at 8 Down. Then look across at 7 Across for the striped animal crossing the yard.

clues.TAIL: Part behind the skunk's body that it can lift

notes.WHITE: A striped skunk's white markings stand out against its black fur. The stripes can vary in width and may extend onto the tail.
notes.NIGHT: A skunk often comes out at night to look for food. In dim light, the pale stripes can stand out more than the darker fur around them.
notes.GRASS: Short yard grass leaves the skunk's dark body and pale stripes easier to see. Taller grass along the edge of a yard can hide most of its body.

small-wild-visitors-5.solvingTip: Begin with the place a mother carries her young at 8 Down. Its crossing at 9 Across can help you spell the name of this nighttime animal.

clues.POUCH: Pocket on a mother opossum's belly that holds her young
clues.TAIL: Long part behind the opossum's body
clues.PAW: Foot the opossum uses to grip a branch

notes.TAIL: An opossum's mostly bare tail can help it keep its balance. The animal also grips branches with its feet.
notes.NIGHT: An opossum that rests in a sheltered place by day may climb after dark. In this scene, its paws help it hold onto the branch at night.
notes.TREE: A tree can give an opossum a place to climb away from the ground. Smaller branches connected to the trunk can serve as routes across the tree.

birds-to-recognize-2.solvingTip: Try the color clue at 2 Across for the shade of a clear sky. It crosses the part of the oak where the bird can land at 2 Down.

notes.WHITE: A blue jay has pale or white underparts. White markings on the wings and tail can also stand out against the darker blue feathers.
notes.BRANCH: A blue jay can grip an oak branch while it looks around. The acorn is part of the oak's crop, and the branch gives the bird a place to pause.
notes.FEATHER: Tiny structures inside a blue jay's feathers scatter light in a way that looks blue to us. The white markings sit beside that blue on parts of its wings and tail.

birds-to-recognize-3.solvingTip: Look for the tiny part of a plant that the birds pick up at 8 Down. Its crossing at 9 Across asks for the action of settling on a stem.

clues.PERCH: Settle on a stem or branch
clues.YELLOW: Bright feather color of a male goldfinch in spring
clues.BIRD: Feathered animal such as the goldfinch

notes.YELLOW: A male American goldfinch often has bright yellow feathers and dark wings in spring and summer. Its plumage can look duller in winter.
notes.BEAK: A goldfinch's short, pointed beak can pick seeds from between the dry parts of a flower head. A single seed can then be opened in that beak.
notes.BIRD: A goldfinch is small enough to perch on the stem of a dry seed head. It can pick out seeds while holding itself steady on the plant.

birds-to-recognize-4.solvingTip: Find the short action for taking a little drink at 3 Across. Then look at the crossing for the part that keeps the bird in the air at 1 Down.

clues.SUGAR: Sweet ingredient often added to water for a bird feeder

notes.SUGAR: Flower nectar already contains sugar. In this garden scene it is the sweetness that draws the bird to the blossoms.
notes.WATER: Plain water dissolves sugar in a hummingbird feeder. The flowers in the same scene make their own sweet liquid, called nectar.
notes.FLOWER: The red flower is a source of nectar for the hummingbird. A feeder nearby can hold a separate sugar-and-water mixture.

birds-to-recognize-5.solvingTip: Start with the shape of the turkey's spread-out tail at 1 Down. The crossing at 4 Across asks for another feathered part used in flight.

notes.SEED: A wild turkey can pick up seeds as it walks along the edge of the woods. It may scratch among fallen leaves to uncover them.
notes.WING: A wild turkey often walks along the ground, and can also use its wings to fly up to a tree to roost. Its tail feathers spread into the broad fan.
notes.BEAK: A turkey uses its beak to pick up exposed seeds and bits of food. Its feet do the scratching that brings some of those pieces into view.

clues.WING: Feathered part a turkey can spread to fly up to a tree
clues.BEAK: Hard mouthpart a turkey uses to pick up food

beside-the-water.solvingTip: Try the barrier the beaver can build across the stream at 3 Across. At 2 Down, its crossing leads to the word for the beaver's home.

notes.TREE: A beaver can gnaw through the base of a small tree with its front teeth. It can use branches from the fallen tree as material for a dam or lodge.
notes.TAIL: A beaver swims with its broad tail helping it steer. It can slap the water with that tail when it is alarmed.

clues.TREE: Plant with a woody trunk that a beaver can gnaw through

beside-the-water-2.solvingTip: Find the familiar word for moving through the river at 1 Across. Its crossing at 2 Down asks what the otter moves through.

clues.WATER: Liquid in the river where the otter swims
clues.ROCK: Piece of stone at the edge of the river

notes.WATER: The otter can slide into the water and swim after a fish. On the bank its paws help it travel over land.
notes.ROCK: A rock on the riverbank can give the otter a foothold before it slides into the water. You may see just the top if the river is running high.
notes.RIVER: The river carries water along a channel. After sliding in, the otter can use its feet and tail to steer through the current.

beside-the-water-3.solvingTip: Start at 5 Down with the action that takes the bird headfirst into the water. It crosses the long bird name at 6 Across.

notes.WATER: From a branch over the pond, a kingfisher can look down through the water for a fish. Its splash comes when it dives.
notes.BRANCH: The branch above the pond is the kingfisher's perch. From there the bird can watch for movement in the water before leaving the branch to dive.
notes.POND: The pond is the still water the kingfisher looks into from its perch. Small ripples on the surface can make a fish harder to see from above.

clues.WATER: Liquid a kingfisher dives into for a fish
clues.BRANCH: Tree limb a kingfisher can perch on above a pond
clues.POND: Body of still water below the kingfisher's perch

beside-the-water-4.solvingTip: Find the short word for the tall bird's walking limb at 6 Down. Then try the crossing about how deep the water is at 4 Across.

notes.WATER: A heron can stand in shallow water with its body held well above the surface. Its legs let it look down for fish without having to swim.
notes.WING: A heron spreads broad wings to lift away from the water. In flight a heron usually holds its neck bent back and lets its long legs trail behind.
notes.SHALLOW: In shallow water, the bottom is close to the surface. The heron can take slow steps along the bottom while it looks down for fish.

clues.WING: Broad feathered part a heron spreads to take flight

beside-the-water-5.solvingTip: Look for the broad floating leaf at 1 Down. Its crossing at 3 Across names the still body of water that holds it.

clues.HOVER: Stay in one spot in the air above the pond
clues.WING: One of four thin parts a dragonfly uses to fly
clues.PAD: Broad floating leaf of a water lily
clues.WATER: Liquid a lily pad floats on
clues.INSECT: Kind of six-legged animal that includes a dragonfly
clues.STEM: Plant stalk that can reach from below the pond's surface

notes.WATER: Dragonflies often fly over water because their young develop below the surface. The adults in this scene hover above the lily pads.
notes.INSECT: A dragonfly is an insect with two pairs of wings. It can hover over a pond and then change direction quickly to catch smaller insects.
notes.STEM: A water lily's flower grows on a stalk that reaches toward the surface. The floating pad is a leaf with a long stalk of its own.

looking-at-the-shore-3.solvingTip: Find the short word for the salt water beyond the rocks at 1 Across. Its crossing at 1 Down helps you name the animal resting there.

notes.WATER: The seals can dive into the water for fish and come back onto the rock to rest. Their flippers help them move between the two places.
notes.ROCK: A broad rock above the water gives seals room to rest out of the sea. As the tide rises, there may be less dry surface to lie on.

clues.WATER: Liquid a seal swims through to catch fish
clues.ROCK: Large stone where seals can rest

looking-at-the-shore-4.solvingTip: Look at 1 Down for the hard mouthpart above the pelican's pouch. It shares a letter with the liquid below the bird at 3 Across.

clues.POUCH: Stretchy pocket below a pelican's bill
clues.WATER: What a pelican drains from its bill after catching fish
clues.BEAK: Long hard mouthpart with a pouch under it in a pelican

notes.WHITE: An American white pelican has a mostly white body and dark wing tips that are especially easy to see in flight. The pouch is beneath the bill.
notes.WATER: A pelican's pouch can take in water with a catch of fish. It can drain the water from its bill before swallowing the fish.
notes.BEAK: The pelican's beak is long and has a pouch of loose skin beneath its lower half. The pouch can open wide as the bird scoops up a fish.

looking-at-the-shore-5.solvingTip: Start with the shore grains under the bird's feet at 5 Across. Its crossing helps you spell the long shorebird name at 1 Down.

notes.SHORE: As small waves slide back, they leave a thin band of wet sand along the shore. Sandpipers can follow that band as they run and look for food.
notes.SAND: As a wave draws back, it exposes wet sand where sandpipers probe for tiny animals. The next wave may wash over the spot where they were feeding.

clues.SAND: Loose grains left wet after a wave rolls back

trees-and-their-fruit.solvingTip: Find the flat part that makes a maple seed spin at 1 Across. A crossing leads to the place where the seed lands at 2 Down.

clues.FALL: Move down from the branch to the ground
clues.SEED: Small part inside a maple's winged fruit that can grow into a tree

notes.BRANCH: The maple branch supports a cluster of seeds while they develop. After they come loose, their papery wings help them spin as they fall.
notes.SEED: The seed sits in a small pouch at the base of the maple's papery wing. The wing helps it spin away from the branch as it falls.
notes.SHADE: A maple's leaves cast shade underneath the branches. A falling seed can spin through that shaded space before it reaches the ground.

trees-and-their-fruit-2.solvingTip: Start with the short word for the food that has a hard shell at 1 Across. The crossing at 2 Down tells you what it grows on.

clues.NUT: Edible part inside a walnut's hard shell
clues.SHADE: Cool area under the walnut tree, out of direct sun

notes.BRANCH: A walnut develops on a branch before it is picked or falls. On the table, you can crack its shell to reach the edible kernel.
notes.SHADE: Shade from the walnut tree can reach the picnic table. The leaves reduce the direct sun where people are sitting, leaving the light softer over the table.
notes.SHELL: A walnut shell has a line where its two halves meet. Cracking along that line can help you lift out a larger piece of the kernel.

trees-and-their-fruit-3.solvingTip: Look at 9 Down for what a flexible branch does when it curves downward. It crosses the land along the creek at 9 Across.

clues.BEND: Curve as a long willow branch does over the creek
clues.WATER: What flows under the willow branches
clues.STREAM: Small waterway flowing under the willow

notes.WATER: The flexible branches of a willow can hang low over a creek. The water keeps flowing underneath even when the breeze moving the branches dies down.
notes.GREEN: The new willow leaves can give the branches a light green look in spring. Long clusters of those narrow leaves hang toward the creek.
notes.STREAM: The stream flows under the hanging willow branches. The bank is the strip of land alongside it where the tree can take root.

trees-and-their-fruit-4.solvingTip: Try the covering on the outside of the trunk at 2 Across. A crossing helps start the name of the pale-barked tree at 2 Down.

clues.PEEL: Come away in a thin layer, as birch bark does
clues.PAPER: Writing material that thin birch bark can resemble

notes.BRANCH: A birch branch joins the trunk and carries leaves out toward the light. On birches with white bark, younger twigs near the tips can have a darker surface.
notes.PAPER: Thin layers of birch bark can peel back like sheets of paper. Here paper describes the bark's appearance. The pale layer is still part of the tree.
notes.SHADE: In a wooded spot, trunks can sit in shade while upper branches catch the sun. The pale bark of a birch can still be easy to pick out among darker trees.

trees-and-their-fruit-5.solvingTip: Start with the short word for what is inside the hard shell at 11 Across. Then try the crossing at 7 Down for how the prickly case opens.

clues.FALL: Drop from a tree, as a ripe nut does
clues.SHELL: Smooth brown covering of the nut inside its prickly case

notes.BRANCH: The chestnut grows inside a prickly case on the branch. As the case ripens and splits, the smooth nut can fall to the ground.
notes.TREE: A chestnut tree can have long leaves with toothed edges. Those edges give you something to look for even before the prickly cases open.
notes.SHELL: The prickly case around a chestnut opens as it ripens. Inside, each nut has its own smooth brown shell.

quiet-outdoor-moments.solvingTip: Look for the ripe-tomato color at 11 Down. It crosses a second rainbow color at 10 Across, the one you see in leaves.

notes.YELLOW: In a usual rainbow, yellow lies between orange and green. The curved band can be visible while rain is still falling farther away.
notes.GREEN: Green sits next to yellow on a rainbow's cooler side. The arc shows those color bands most clearly when you look toward a passing shower with the sun behind you.
notes.RAINBOW: A rainbow can show over the field when sunlight reaches drops from a passing shower. Look toward the rain with the sun behind you.

clues.GREEN: Rainbow color next to yellow on its cooler side
clues.RAINBOW: Colored arc that can appear after a shower

quiet-outdoor-moments-2.solvingTip: Start with the early light that arrives before sunrise at 4 Down. Its crossing helps you spell the word for an image you can see on still water at 7 Across.

clues.SOFT: Gentle, like morning light through the mist
clues.SHORE: Land at the edge of a misty lake

notes.SOFT: Mist can make the morning light look muted, the way a lamp looks through a thin curtain.
notes.SHORE: The shore gives you a place to stand and look out across the lake. In low mist the near shore can stay visible while the far bank fades from view.
notes.SUN: As the sun climbs, the air over the lake may warm enough for the mist to thin. The far shore can gradually come back into view.

quiet-outdoor-moments-3.solvingTip: Find the word for one little bit of water at 2 Across. The crossing at 2 Down names the drops you see on the grass in the morning.

notes.LIGHT: At first light, tiny drops of dew can reflect the sun. That is what makes some drops sparkle while the grass around them still looks dark.
notes.GRASS: Drops of dew can sit along the narrow blades of grass. They may dry away first in the parts of the meadow that the morning sun reaches.
notes.STEM: Dew can gather at places where leaves meet the grass stem. That stem can also hold a seed head above the shorter blades.

clues.LIGHT: Brightness that makes drops of dew sparkle
clues.GRASS: Narrow-leaved growth that can hold dew on its blades
clues.STEM: Stalk on which blades of grass can grow

quiet-outdoor-moments-4.solvingTip: Try the word at 9 Across that tells how you can see the stones through the water. It crosses the clue for a small wave at 4 Down.

clues.SAND: Fine grains that can settle between brook pebbles

notes.STREAM: A stream keeps moving through its channel even where the water looks clear and calm. Look for little ripples where it passes over a line of pebbles.
notes.STONE: A stone that sticks up into the brook can send the water around its sides. Smaller stones may stay fully below the surface where the water is clear.

quiet-outdoor-moments-5.solvingTip: Start with the moving air at 9 Across, which you can hear in the grass. Its crossing names the open, grassy place at 6 Down.

clues.BEND: Curve toward the ground when the air moves
clues.GREEN: Common color of meadow grass in warm weather
clues.WIND: Moving air that makes meadow grasses lean

notes.GREEN: A meadow can be green lower down while the tops of some stalks look tan. The lighter tips may carry the grass seeds.
notes.GRASS: The sound in the meadow can come from grass blades rubbing together. The taller stems bend a little with each passing breeze.
notes.WIND: You can see the direction of the wind by watching which way the grass leans. When the air eases, some stems can straighten again.

night-outdoors.solvingTip: Find the brief burst of light at 2 Across. The crossing at 1 Down asks for the verb meaning to shine with a softer light.

clues.WING: Thin part an insect uses to fly
clues.SUMMER: Warm season when fireflies often flash over a lawn
clues.INSECT: Kind of six-legged animal that includes fireflies

notes.SUMMER: On a summer evening, the flashes can become easier to see as the lawn darkens. Fireflies use the flashes as signals to other fireflies.
notes.GRASS: The grass gives the tiny flashes a darker background as evening falls. A firefly can lift off above the lawn, where the flash is easier to see.
notes.INSECT: A firefly is a kind of beetle. The glow comes from its body, and the wings let it carry that flash above the grass.

night-outdoors-4.solvingTip: Try the short name at 7 Across for the flying mammal. It crosses the time of day when the animal is active at 2 Down.

notes.NIGHT: Dusk is when daylight is fading. Bats that start hunting then can stay out at night, when they find insects even in the dark.
notes.INSECT: Some bats catch flying insects such as moths above a garden. A moth has six legs, while the bat has wings made from skin stretched along its forelimbs.

clues.NIGHT: Dark part of the day that follows dusk

night-outdoors-5.solvingTip: Look at 2 Down for the object that gives off light near the front door. Its crossing names the covered area where the moth rests at 5 Across.

clues.LAMP: Fixture that gives off light beside the front door
clues.WING: Broad part the moth uses to fly
clues.WINDOW: Opening with glass near the porch lamp
clues.SHADE: Cover that fits around a porch lamp
clues.INSECT: Kind of six-legged creature that includes moths

notes.WINDOW: The porch light can make the glass of the nearby window glow from the outside. A moth may rest on the frame or the siding beside it.
notes.SHADE: In this scene, shade means the cover around the porch lamp. It can direct the light downward, where a moth may be easier to notice.
notes.INSECT: A moth is an insect with wings covered in tiny scales. Those scales can look like fine dust when a few rub off.

breakfast-from-the-stove.solvingTip: Look at 9 Across for what you crack before whisking. One of its letters helps with the dairy spread that goes into the warm skillet at 7 Down.

notes.PLATE: The frying pan is where the eggs cook. The plate is where you put the finished scramble so it can go straight to the table.
notes.BUTTER: A little butter melted in the pan coats the surface for the eggs. The whisk is used earlier, while the eggs are still in the mixing bowl.
notes.WHISK: A few strokes with the whisk break the yolks and mix them through the whites. The eggs are ready to pour when the mixture looks evenly yellow.

clues.BUTTER: Dairy fat often melted in a pan before eggs go in

breakfast-from-the-stove-2.solvingTip: Try the action that turns a pancake over at 6 Down. Its crossing helps you name the flat vessel it cooks in at 8 Across.

notes.PLATE: A flat plate gives the stack a steady base. It also catches syrup that runs down the sides when you cut into the pancakes.
notes.BUTTER: A pat of butter can soften on the top pancake. The syrup can then spread over the top and run down the sides of the stack.
notes.FORK: A fork's prongs can hold down a piece of pancake while it is cut. They can then lift the soft piece with some syrup still on it.

clues.BUTTER: Cream-based spread that melts on warm pancakes

breakfast-from-the-stove-5.solvingTip: Start with the liquid cooking fat that keeps the grated potato from sticking at 8 Across. A crossing gives you a letter for the layered vegetable at 5 Down.

clues.BROWN: Cook until a darker crust forms on the potatoes
clues.PLATE: Flat dish you serve hash browns on
clues.ONION: Layered vegetable sometimes grated into hash browns
clues.POTATO: Starchy vegetable grated to make hash browns

notes.PLATE: Hash browns can be served on one side of a plate next to the eggs. The crisp outside is made in the pan before the potatoes are served.
notes.ONION: Grating onion with the potatoes spreads its flavor through the hash browns. Small pieces cook along with the potatoes as the outside crisps.
notes.POTATO: Grate the potato into thin shreds so they can brown together. Pressing out some of the moisture first helps the outside crisp in the pan.

bowls-of-soup.solvingTip: Find the deep vessel the soup cooks in at 1 Down. Its crossing points to the smaller round dish that gets carried to the table at 3 Across.

notes.SPOON: A soup spoon can hold broth and a few noodles at once. The deeper ladle moves a larger amount from the pot into the bowl.
notes.CARROT: Small carrot slices soften in chicken broth as the soup cooks. Their orange color makes them easy to pick out among the noodles.
notes.BROTH: Chicken broth is the liquid around the noodles and vegetables. It carries the taste of the chicken into spoonfuls that have no piece of meat.

clues.SPOON: Utensil that can hold a bite of noodles and broth
clues.CARROT: Orange root that can be sliced into chicken noodle soup

bowls-of-soup-2.solvingTip: Start at 9 Down with the color of a ripe tomato. A crossing leads to the crisp dry snack served with the soup at 8 Across.

notes.SPOON: A spoon can stir the tomato soup all the way down to the bottom of the pot. At the table, small spoonfuls give you a chance to let the hot soup cool.
notes.TOMATO: As tomatoes cook, their pieces soften enough to blend into a smooth soup. A few leaves of basil can add a fresh scent just before serving.
notes.BOWL: The pot holds the whole batch, while the bowl holds one lunch serving. Its rim leaves room to set down the spoon between bites.

clues.TOMATO: Red fruit cooked until soft for a smooth soup
clues.BOWL: Round dish that holds one serving of tomato soup

bowls-of-soup-3.solvingTip: Look for the small green vegetable that gives this dish its name at 10 Down. That word crosses the liquid dish it goes into at 9 Across.

clues.BONE: Hard part of a ham that can flavor the broth
clues.HAM: Cured pork simmered with the peas
clues.CARROT: Orange root vegetable sometimes diced into split pea soup

notes.WATER: Dried split peas absorb some of the water as they cook. As they soften and break apart, they help turn the cooking liquid into thick soup.
notes.SPOON: Split peas soften until the soup is thick enough to cling to the back of a spoon. A ladle is handy when you are filling an entire bowl.
notes.CARROT: Diced carrot can cook in the pot while the split peas soften. The pieces stay visible in the green soup even after the peas have broken down.

bowls-of-soup-4.solvingTip: Try the cooking vessel that holds the broth at 4 Across. Its crossing names the deep dish the broth is served in at 3 Down.

notes.CARROT: Cut the carrot into pieces about the same size so it softens evenly in the stock. Its small pieces can be ladled out with the beans and corn.
notes.BOWL: A deep soup bowl holds stock as well as the vegetables and beans. A ladle can bring up a little of each from the stockpot for every serving.
notes.WARM: Warm describes how the soup feels when served. You can let a ladleful cool in the bowl before bringing it to the table.

clues.BOWL: Deep dish that holds a serving of vegetables and stock
clues.WARM: Pleasantly heated, as soup may be when served

bowls-of-soup-5.solvingTip: Try the short temperature word at 9 Down. The crossing at 10 Across asks what heat does to the cheese.

notes.CHEESE: A slice of toast can float on the soup and support the grated cheese. As it melts, the cheese spreads over the toast and browns at the top.
notes.SPOON: The spoon can break through the softened toast and lift the onion broth underneath. A little melted cheese may come up in the same bite.
notes.BROTH: Broth is the liquid base of onion soup. Onion slices soften in it, then toast and cheese can be added on top.

clues.CHEESE: Dairy topping that melts over toast in onion soup
clues.SPOON: Bowl-ended utensil used to eat onion soup
clues.BROTH: Savory liquid under the toast in onion soup

sandwich-counter.solvingTip: Start with what turns the sandwich to its other side at 6 Across. Then use one of its letters for the single piece cut from the bread at 4 Down.

clues.FLIP: Turn the sandwich over to cook the other side

notes.CHEESE: Cheese is the filling that softens between the bread slices. The butter goes on the outsides so the bread browns against the skillet.
notes.SLICE: The cheese can go on as a thin slice so it covers much of the bread. The bread slices hold that filling on either side as it melts.
notes.BUTTER: Butter the bread on the sides that will touch the skillet. Those surfaces crisp as the cheese softens between the slices.

sandwich-counter-2.solvingTip: Find the glass container at 2 Down. Its crossing at 2 Across names the fruit spread on one side of the sandwich.

notes.BREAD: Soft bread holds the two spreads together. Putting peanut butter on the bread first can help keep the jelly from soaking straight into the slice.
notes.CRUST: The crust is the baked edge around the soft middle of each bread slice. It can stay on a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, or be trimmed away after the sandwich is assembled.
notes.SANDWICH: Peanut butter and jelly can be spread on separate bread slices before they are brought together. The sandwich can then be cut across the middle for two smaller portions.

clues.BREAD: Baked food that holds the peanut butter and jelly
clues.CRUST: Outer baked edge of the bread in a sandwich
clues.SLICE: Flat piece of bread cut from a loaf

sandwich-counter-3.solvingTip: Picture the little pointed stick that holds the layers together at 10 Across. A crossing helps with the flat piece of bread at 7 Down.

clues.PICK: Small pointed stick that holds the sandwich layers together
clues.TOMATO: Juicy red fruit often sliced into a club sandwich

notes.PLATE: A broad plate can hold the pieces after a club sandwich is cut. The flat surface keeps the layered pieces easy to pick up.
notes.CRUST: The edges of each toast slice are its crust. Those firmer edges can help a tall club sandwich stay tidy when it is cut into quarters.
notes.TOMATO: A tomato slice adds juice to the layers of a club sandwich. Putting it next to the lettuce can help keep that juice off the toast.

sandwich-counter-4.solvingTip: Look at 5 Across for the metal container the tuna is packed in. It crosses the serving dish that holds the sandwich at 2 Down.

notes.PLATE: The tuna mixture is made in a bowl, then spread on the rye. A plate is what you set the finished sandwich on when you serve it.
notes.SLICE: One slice of rye goes below the tuna and one above it. The word slice describes the flat pieces of bread, while the tuna is the spread between them.
notes.ONION: A little finely chopped onion can give tuna salad a crunch and a sharper taste. Smaller pieces spread through the filling on the rye.

clues.PLATE: Flat dish you serve a tuna sandwich on
clues.SLICE: One flat piece of rye bread for a sandwich
clues.ONION: Layered vegetable sometimes chopped into tuna salad

sandwich-counter-5.solvingTip: Start with the temperature of the meatballs at 2 Down. The crossing at 4 Across asks what the cheese does as it warms on top.

notes.PLATE: A long meatball roll can rest flat on a plate. The plate catches any sauce or filling that drops when you pick the roll up.
notes.CHEESE: A thin layer of cheese can melt over the hot meatballs. A longer roll holds the filling in a line so the cheese can cover more than one meatball.
notes.TOMATO: The tomatoes are cooked into the sauce that coats the meatballs. Simmering lets some liquid cook away so the sauce stays in the long roll more easily.

clues.TOMATO: Red fruit that gives the sauce over meatballs its color
clues.ROLL: Long piece of bread that holds a row of meatballs
clues.BREAD: Baked food that makes up the outside of the sandwich

supper-in-the-oven.solvingTip: Try the short clue for what you crack into the meat mixture at 8 Down. Its crossing points to the piece cut from the finished loaf at 7 Across.

notes.PLATE: Bake the loaf in the pan. After it has rested, put the slices on a plate so they can be served one at a time.
notes.SLICE: A slice is a serving cut across the cooked meatloaf. Letting the loaf rest before cutting helps the slices hold together for serving.
notes.ONION: Chopped onion is mixed into the raw meatloaf so the flavor reaches each serving. The pieces soften as the loaf bakes.

clues.ONION: Layered vegetable often chopped into a meatloaf mixture
clues.LOAF: Whole shaped portion of meat before it is sliced

supper-in-the-oven-2.solvingTip: Begin with the white seasoning at 2 Down. Then look at its crossing for the vegetable roasting beside the chicken at 4 Across.

clues.POTATO: Vegetable cut into chunks to roast beside the chicken
clues.JUICE: Liquid released by the chicken as it roasts
clues.FORK: Pronged utensil that can hold a chicken while it is carved
clues.OVEN: Kitchen appliance where the chicken and potatoes roast
clues.SKIN: Outer layer of the chicken that turns brown as it roasts

notes.JUICE: The chicken releases liquid as it roasts. That liquid collects in the pan and can flavor the potatoes beside the bird.
notes.POTATO: Chunks of potato can roast in the same pan as the chicken. A similar size helps them soften at about the same rate while their cut sides brown.
notes.FORK: A carving fork can steady the roasted chicken as pieces are cut. Its long prongs give you a place to hold the bird while keeping your hand above the pan.

supper-in-the-oven-3.solvingTip: Find the container that holds the peppers in the oven at 9 Down. It shares a square with the topping spooned over them at 10 Across.

clues.PAN: Shallow vessel that holds the stuffed peppers in the oven
clues.CHEESE: Dairy topping that can melt over a stuffed pepper
clues.SPOON: Bowl-ended utensil for putting stuffing into a hollow pepper
clues.SAUCE: Seasoned liquid that can bake around a stuffed pepper

notes.CHEESE: Cheese can go on top of the pepper after the rice and meat filling is packed inside. Its browned surface is separate from the stuffing below.
notes.SPOON: Use the spoon's bowl to transfer a little stuffing at a time. Its rounded back can settle the rice and meat into the hollow space.
notes.SAUCE: Sauce can go around the stuffed pepper before it bakes. It pools at the bottom of the pan, where you can spoon some onto each portion at supper.

supper-in-the-oven-4.solvingTip: Look for the white liquid added to the cheese mixture at 6 Down. Its crossing helps you spell the long pasta name at 6 Across.

clues.SPOON: Utensil used to stir the cheese sauce
clues.BUTTER: Dairy fat melted at the start of many cheese sauces
clues.BAKE: Cook the macaroni and cheese in an oven

notes.SPOON: The rounded end helps move sauce over the pasta. For serving, it can lift several small pieces together.
notes.CHEESE: The cheese melts into the sauce, which coats the elbow macaroni. A little on top can brown in the oven while the sauce underneath stays creamy.
notes.BUTTER: Butter is often melted first when making the sauce. Stirring flour into it gives a base for the milk and cheese that go in afterward.

supper-in-the-oven-5.solvingTip: Think of the shallow baking vessel at 6 Across. It crosses the name for the evening meal at 1 Down.

clues.PAN: Shallow baking vessel that holds the lasagna layers
clues.SLICE: Single portion cut through a pan of layered pasta
clues.TOMATO: Red fruit often cooked into sauce for lasagna

notes.CHEESE: Ricotta can be spread into a soft layer between sheets of pasta. Other cheeses can go over the top and melt as the lasagna bakes.
notes.SLICE: Cut through all the layers to make a slice of lasagna. A serving often has straight sides because the lasagna is baked in a rectangular pan.
notes.TOMATO: A thin layer of tomato sauce under the first pasta sheet keeps the bottom of the lasagna moist. More sauce can go between the noodle and vegetable layers.

supper-on-the-stove.solvingTip: Try the deep vessel you boil the noodles in at 3 Down. It crosses the general name for foods like spaghetti at 3 Across.

notes.CHEESE: A little grated cheese can be scattered over the sauce just before serving. Small shreds spread over the strands more evenly than one large piece would.
notes.TOMATO: Crushed tomatoes can become a sauce that clings to spaghetti. Simmering softens the pieces and lets the sauce thicken before it meets the noodles.
notes.PASTA: Spaghetti is a pasta made in long strands. Twirling a few strands around a fork lets you lift them with some of the sauce.

clues.CHEESE: Dairy food that can be grated over spaghetti
clues.PASTA: Food such as spaghetti or penne

supper-on-the-stove-2.solvingTip: Look first for the part that covers the rice while it cooks at 3 Down. Then try the crossing for the container you serve it in at 5 Across.

notes.WHITE: White rice has had its outer bran removed. The same type of rice can also be sold as brown rice with that layer left on.
notes.WATER: Rice takes up water as it cooks. Keeping the pot covered holds in much of the steam while the grains soften.
notes.RICE: A cup of dry rice takes up more room once the grains have cooked. Leave space in the pot for them to swell as they soften.

clues.WHITE: Color of rice with the outer bran removed
clues.RICE: Grain that can be steamed and served as a side

supper-on-the-stove-3.solvingTip: Picture the deep container on the stove at 3 Across. A crossing takes you to the word for the meal it provides at 1 Down.

notes.ONION: Onion can cook at the bottom of the pot before the beans and liquid go in. It softens and adds flavor to the chili as the whole mixture simmers.

supper-on-the-stove-4.solvingTip: Begin with the cooking fat you pour into the skillet at 7 Across. Its crossing names what you do to give the pork a darker surface at 4 Down.

clues.BROWN: Cook the pork until its outside darkens

notes.PLATE: The plate holds the cooked chops after they come out of the frying pan. Pick them up at the thicker end with tongs so they stay steady during the move.
notes.SALT: Salt can be sprinkled over the surface of a chop before it goes into the pan. The small grains dissolve into moisture on the meat as it cooks.
notes.OIL: A thin layer of oil helps the pork chops brown without sticking as you turn them. It goes into the frying pan before the chops.

supper-on-the-stove-5.solvingTip: Try the green herb the fish is served with at 4 Across. It crosses the action of using a fork to separate a bite of the cooked fish at 3 Down.

clues.DILL: Feathery green herb served with salmon
clues.FORK: Pronged utensil that can lift a flake of cooked fish
clues.LEMON: Sour yellow fruit often served in a wedge beside salmon

notes.PLATE: Set the wedge on the plate beside the salmon. That lets you squeeze lemon over the part of the fish you are about to eat.
notes.FORK: A fork can tease a cooked salmon flake away along a natural seam. The tender piece can then be lifted without having to cut across the whole fillet.
notes.LEMON: A lemon wedge gives you a piece of peel to hold while you squeeze the cut side over the salmon. Any seeds left in the wedge can be removed before serving.

salads-to-share.solvingTip: Look at 5 Across for what you do to take the skin off the potato. Its crossing at 2 Down names the crisp vegetable with long stalks.

clues.ONION: Layered vegetable that can add crunch to potato salad
clues.POTATO: Starchy vegetable cooked and cubed for a picnic salad

notes.ONION: Potato salad can include finely diced onion. Its small crisp pieces give a different bite from the softer cubes of cooked potato.
notes.CHILL: Chilling the potato salad gives the dressing time to coat the potatoes and other ingredients. The salad is served cold for the picnic.
notes.POTATO: The potatoes are cooked before being dressed for the salad. A firm kind of potato can hold its cubed shape as you fold in the other ingredients.

salads-to-share-2.solvingTip: Try the short name for the shredded salad at 4 Across. Its crossing goes into the name of the leafy head you shred at 2 Down.

notes.WHITE: Some cabbage called white cabbage looks pale green on the outside, with lighter leaves inside. Its shreds stand out next to orange carrot in the salad.
notes.CHILL: Coleslaw can chill after the shreds are tossed with dressing. Cooling the bowl helps it stay cold while it is set out to serve.
notes.CARROT: A grated carrot makes thin orange shreds that mix easily through the cabbage. Using a coarse grater leaves pieces with a little more crunch.

clues.CARROT: Orange root that can be shredded into coleslaw
clues.SALAD: Cold side dish made with shredded cabbage and carrots

salads-to-share-3.solvingTip: Start with the fresh herb sprinkled over the cucumber at 5 Across. A crossing leads to the tart liquid in the dressing at 4 Down.

notes.SLICE: Thin cuts across a cucumber make round slices. The pale center with its seeds is visible in each one.
notes.FORK: Slide a fork under a thin cucumber slice to lift it with a little dressing. The gaps between the prongs let extra liquid drip back into the bowl.
notes.SALT: A little salt seasons the cucumber slices and can draw moisture from their cut surfaces. The dill and vinegar give the dressing its other flavors.

clues.SLICE: Thin round piece cut across a cucumber
clues.SALT: White seasoning sprinkled on cucumber slices

salads-to-share-4.solvingTip: Begin with the part of the dressing that mixes with vinegar at 10 Down. It crosses the vegetable whose layers come apart as you cut it at 9 Across.

clues.SPOON: Utensil for tossing the beans with the dressing
clues.WAX: Word for the yellow kind in a three-bean salad
clues.ONION: Layered vegetable often sliced into three-bean salad
clues.CHILL: Cool the bean salad in a refrigerator before serving

notes.SPOON: A large spoon lifts the beans from the bottom of the dish. That motion brings dressing up through the salad.
notes.ONION: Thin slices of onion can soak up some of the vinegar dressing as the salad chills. Red onion is one way to add color alongside the beans.
notes.CHILL: Chill describes putting the mixed bean salad in the refrigerator. A little time there lets the vinegar dressing settle around the beans.

salads-to-share-5.solvingTip: Try the deep dish that holds the cut fruit at 5 Across. Its crossing names the citrus fruit with segments at 6 Down.

clues.BOWL: Deep round dish that holds the mixed fruit

notes.SWEET: Ripe banana and melon bring their own sweetness to a fruit salad. Cutting several fruits into small pieces gives a mix of flavors in one spoonful.
notes.CHILL: Chill the mixed fruit after it goes into the bowl. Cut pieces can cool together in the refrigerator and be served with the juice they release.
notes.APPLE: An apple cut into small pieces gives a fruit salad some crunch. A pale cut side may darken after it has been exposed to the air for a while.

vegetable-side-dishes.solvingTip: Start with the shallow vessel that holds the carrots in the oven at 9 Down. Its crossing helps with the thin shiny coating made with honey at 10 Across.

notes.CARROT: Cut the carrots into pieces of a similar thickness so they finish roasting at about the same time. The light honey glaze coats the pieces as they cook.
notes.FORK: Use the tip of a fork to check a thick carrot piece. If the prongs go in easily, the inside has softened as well as the glazed surface.
notes.ROOT: A carrot's thick root is the part you peel and roast. Its narrow tip may soften sooner in the pan if the pieces are left uneven.

clues.CARROT: Orange root vegetable you might roast with honey
clues.FORK: Pronged utensil used to check whether a roasted carrot is tender
clues.ROOT: Part of a carrot plant that can be peeled and roasted

vegetable-side-dishes-2.solvingTip: Try the word for the long green case that holds the seeds at 3 Down. It crosses the nut that is toasted and scattered over the beans at 4 Across.

clues.TOAST: Heat the almonds in a dry pan until lightly browned
clues.POD: Long green case that holds the bean seeds

notes.SPOON: A serving spoon can lift green beans together with the loose pieces of almond. The toasted nuts are the smaller, crisp pieces mixed in with the beans.
notes.NUT: Almond is the nut used in this side dish. Toasted slices bring a little crunch to the cooked green beans.
notes.PAN: A shallow pan lets almond slices spread out while they toast. The thin edges can turn golden before the thicker centers do.

vegetable-side-dishes-3.solvingTip: Look at 3 Across for the cover that holds steam in. It crosses the word describing broccoli that is easy to bite at 1 Down.

keeping-food-fresh.solvingTip: Try the container that carries the lunch at 7 Across. One crossing leads to the utensil packed for scooping food at 5 Down.

notes.HANDLE: The handle of a lunch box carries the weight of the packed food. The lid keeps those items inside once it is fastened.
notes.FRUIT: The fruit in a packed lunch can be a whole apple. Packing it whole keeps the cut surfaces from browning before the meal.
notes.SANDWICH: A sandwich fits flat inside a lunch box and can be wrapped to keep the filling together. Placing it above heavier items helps the bread hold its shape.

clues.HANDLE: Part you grip to lift a lunch box

keeping-food-fresh-2.solvingTip: Start with the hard form water takes in the freezer at 9 Across. Its crossing helps name the action of putting one labeled container above another at 7 Down.

notes.SHELF: A freezer shelf supports containers as they stack. Put the dates where you can read them from the front, even after another box goes on top.
notes.LABEL: A freezer label tells you what is inside a closed container. A dry spot on the side or lid gives adhesive tape a surface it can stick to before freezing.
notes.BOX: A freezer-safe box with straight sides can fit neatly beside others of the same size. A lid keeps the food covered and gives the box above it a flat place to rest.

clues.SHELF: Flat surface inside a freezer that supports containers
clues.LABEL: Tag showing what food is inside a freezer container
clues.BOX: Rigid container for stacking food in the freezer

keeping-food-fresh-3.solvingTip: Find the part you open before putting groceries away at 2 Down. It crosses the everyday name for the whole appliance at 6 Across.

clues.DOOR: Part you swing open to reach the chilled shelves
clues.DRAWER: Pull-out section of the refrigerator for produce
clues.BUTTER: Refrigerated dairy spread made from cream
clues.SHELF: Horizontal surface inside the fridge for holding groceries

notes.DRAWER: Pulling the drawer out gives you room to reach produce. It sits below the shelves where bottles and jars can stand.
notes.CHEESE: Putting the cheese back in its wrapper after opening keeps the exposed edge from drying out as quickly. The wrapped piece can go on a shelf with the other chilled food.
notes.BUTTER: Keeping butter wrapped in the fridge helps protect it from the smells of other foods. The wrapper also keeps its exposed surface from drying out too quickly.

keeping-food-fresh-5.solvingTip: Look first for the cover that closes the breadbox at 1 Across. Its crossing names the whole baked bread inside at 1 Down.

clues.CRUMB: Small loose bit that falls from a slice of bread
clues.COUNTER: Kitchen surface a breadbox can sit on

notes.COUNTER: A breadbox can sit on the counter within reach when you make a sandwich. Its lid covers the loaf, while the counter leaves you a flat place to cut a slice.
notes.BREAD: A covered breadbox helps keep the bread from drying out in the open air. If a loaf has been cut, its exposed end can be tucked into a bag before the lid is closed.
notes.CRUST: A loaf's crust is darker and firmer than its crumb, the soft inside revealed when it is sliced. A crisp crust can soften after the loaf sits in a breadbox.

neighborhood-businesses.solvingTip: Look at 10 Across for the small metal piece that fits a lock. One of its letters helps you name the device that cuts a copy at 4 Down.

clues.MACHINE: Device at the hardware store that cuts a copy of a house key
clues.COUNTER: Raised surface where you give the worker a key to copy

notes.METAL: The worker starts with a plain metal blank. Cutting its edge makes the shape that fits the lock.
notes.COUNTER: The counter is where you hand the original key to the hardware worker. The cutting machine can sit behind it on the worker's side.

neighborhood-businesses-2.solvingTip: Try 9 Across for the tool you use to sign the card in ink. Its crossing belongs to the friendly words inside at 4 Down.

notes.PRICE: The price of a greeting card can be printed on the back. Look separately for the envelope in the rack behind the cards.
notes.ENVELOPE: A greeting card needs an envelope wide enough for its fold and corners. Cards on a shop rack often have a matching one tucked behind them.
notes.THANKS: A shop card can carry a printed message of thanks. The blank space inside gives you room to add a short greeting in your own words.

clues.ENVELOPE: Paper holder that fits around a greeting card

neighborhood-businesses-3.solvingTip: Start with the container the parcel goes in at 9 Across. At 7 Down, look for the more specific word for a container made of stiff cardboard.

clues.CARTON: Stiff cardboard container suitable for shipping
clues.BOX: Container you fill before sealing a parcel
clues.COUNTER: Flat surface where a clerk takes a package for shipping
clues.RECEIPT: Record of the shipping charge that may show a tracking number

notes.COUNTER: The shipping counter gives you a flat spot to set down the parcel. The clerk can move it from there to the scale before making the label.
notes.RECEIPT: A shipping receipt may show a tracking number along with the charge. The destination address travels on the parcel's own label.

neighborhood-businesses-4.solvingTip: Find the clear piece that sits in front of one eye at 10 Across. Then use the crossing to name the holder that protects the glasses at 8 Down.

clues.LENS: Clear curved piece you look through in a pair of glasses
clues.MIRROR: Reflective glass used to check how eyeglasses sit on your face

notes.MIRROR: The shop mirror lets you see whether the two lenses look level on your face. A side view can show where the arms sit behind your ears.
notes.EAR: An eyeglass arm can curve behind the ear to stay in place. Its end should rest there without needing to be held by hand.

neighborhood-businesses-5.solvingTip: Try the metal container you open and stir at 12 Across. The crossing at 10 Down asks for the shallow place where you pour a little paint for the roller.

clues.TRAY: Shallow holder you pour paint into for a roller
clues.COLOR: Quality that distinguishes blue paint from green paint

notes.BRUSH: A brush can reach the narrow edge of a wall. A wide roller covers the open surface more quickly.
notes.COLOR: A swatch shows the color of paint. Gloss tells you how shiny the dried surface will look. Two cans can have the same color with different finishes.
notes.PAINT: Paint can look a little different on a wall than it does on a small store swatch. A dry sample lets you see how that coating looks in the room's light.

around-the-town-square.solvingTip: Begin with what you carry the apples home in at 5 Across. It crosses the place the produce was grown at 3 Down.

notes.PRICE: A market sign might list apples by the pound and corn by the ear. The amount named beside each price tells you what that price will buy.
notes.APPLE: At a market stall, two kinds of apple can look alike in their crates. A sign with the variety name can help you recognize the kind you meant to buy.
notes.PEACH: A peach is easiest to recognize by the fine fuzz on its skin. At the market, it can be packed above heavier produce so the ripe fruit keeps its shape.

clues.APPLE: Round orchard fruit a market may sell by the pound

around-the-town-square-2.solvingTip: What time is halfway through the day? Try 6 Across, then use its crossing to name the device on the tower at 3 Down.

clues.HAND: Pointer that moves around the face of the town clock
clues.BRICK: One hard block that can form a wall beneath a town clock
clues.BENCH: Long seat where you can rest below a town clock

notes.CLOCK: At noon, the hour pointer reaches twelve and the minute pointer comes back to the same mark. The chime can announce the hour to people below.
notes.BRICK: Rows of brick can make up the town clock tower's outer wall. From the bench below, you may see the wall's small horizontal lines beneath the round clock face.
notes.BENCH: A bench facing the square gives you a place to rest while you watch the clock. You can also hear its chime from the seat.

around-the-town-square-3.solvingTip: Look for the cloth symbol that moves in the breeze at 3 Across. One crossing leads to the room where neighbors gather at 1 Down.

notes.FLOWER: The flower is the part of the bedding plant that blooms. Planting several colors together gives people something to see on the way into the building.
notes.WINDOW: The front windows look out over the flower beds at the town hall. The beds frame the view at ground level, while the flag stands higher up.
notes.BRICK: Brick can frame the windows and entrance of the town hall. The joints between the separate blocks stay visible behind the flower beds.

clues.BRICK: Baked clay block that can form part of a town hall wall

around-the-town-square-4.solvingTip: Start with the small fastener pressed into the notice board at 4 Down. Its crossing names the kind of gathering the notice might announce at 6 Across.

clues.BOARD: Flat surface where local notices are put up
clues.PHOTO: Picture taken with a camera and pinned beside a notice

notes.GLASS: The glass front protects the pinned announcements. You can read the date through it even when the board's cover is closed.
notes.PHOTO: A photo pinned beside a notice can show what happened at an earlier event. The date on the notice tells when a future event will take place.
notes.FRAME: The frame runs around the notice board and can hold its glass front. The papers are pinned to the board inside that border.

around-the-town-square-5.solvingTip: Picture what someone tosses when making a wish at 1 Down. It shares a square with the broad bowl that catches the fountain water at 6 Across.

notes.WATER: A recirculating fountain lifts water to the spout and catches it again in the basin. A coin dropped in usually settles at the bottom.
notes.STONE: The fountain basin can be carved from stone. Its hard sides keep their shape as water splashes from the spout and collects below.

clues.STONE: Hard rock a fountain basin can be made of

visits-and-gatherings-2.solvingTip: Try the word for a warm embrace at 9 Across. Then use its crossing to name the picture the family takes together at 8 Down.

notes.TABLE: A picnic table gives relatives a shared place to set out food. A separate corner can hold family photos where people can stop to look at them.
notes.FAMILY: A family reunion can bring together relatives from several households. A cousin, an aunt, and an uncle can all be part of the same gathering.
notes.PHOTO: One reunion photo can show relatives from several households together. Taking it before people begin to leave gives more of the group a chance to be in it.

clues.PHOTO: Picture taken with a camera of relatives at a reunion

visits-and-gatherings-3.solvingTip: Start at 7 Down with the word for a friendly, informal talk. Its crossing helps with the name for the place where people meet at 7 Across.

clues.CENTER: Place with rooms for classes, games, and other group activities
clues.DOOR: Movable panel you pass through when entering a meeting room
clues.COFFEE: Hot drink that can be served during a break at the senior center
clues.GAME: Activity with rules, such as checkers

notes.DOOR: The door is the panel you open to enter the center or meeting room. A sign beside it may point out which activity is inside.
notes.COFFEE: At the center, coffee can be set out for people who come to visit or join an activity. The coffee table gives them a place to stop and talk during a break.
notes.GAME: A card game can give people at the senior center something to do together. Dealing everyone in is one way to make room for someone who just arrived.

visits-and-gatherings-4.solvingTip: Find the little label attached to an item at 3 Across. It shares a square with the name of the event where neighbors buy the items at 1 Down.

notes.TABLE: At a yard sale, a table brings small items up where people can look at them easily. A price tag can stay with an item when a shopper picks it up.
notes.PRICE: A tag carries the asking price as a shopper picks up a yard-sale item. When a seller agrees to a bargain, the amount paid can be lower than the tag.
notes.CHANGE: A yard-sale seller may keep a few small bills and coins handy as change. If a five-dollar lamp is paid for with a ten, the buyer gets five dollars back.

clues.TABLE: Raised surface where yard-sale items are set out
clues.CHANGE: Money handed back when a buyer pays more than the price

visits-and-gatherings-5.solvingTip: Look at 9 Down for what helps the newcomers find their way around. A crossing leads to what they might use to wash their hands at 10 Across.

notes.BASKET: The basket keeps small welcome gifts together at the door. A neighborhood map or note can go on top so it is easy to spot.
notes.RIBBON: A ribbon across the basket can hold a welcome card in view. The towels and other useful gifts can be packed below it.
notes.TOWEL: A small hand towel can fit into a basket beside a bar of soap. It gives the new neighbors something ready to use while their own things are still packed.

clues.BASKET: Handled container for holding welcome gifts
clues.TOWEL: Absorbent cloth that might go in a welcome basket beside soap

household-paperwork.solvingTip: Start with the little stack of sheets you pull toward you at 1 Across. Its crossing asks what those sheets are made of at 1 Down.

clues.PAD: Small stack of writing sheets joined at one edge
clues.PENCIL: Erasable writing tool for making a grocery list
clues.GROCERY: ___ list, a note of food and household items to buy

notes.PAPER: A writing pad keeps the sheets together while you add items. You can tear one loose to take it to the store.
notes.PENCIL: A pencil lets you change the grocery list as you check what is already in the cupboard. It also lets you cross out items as they go into the cart.
notes.GROCERY: Grocery is the word that describes the kind of list in this scene. It can include food like eggs and milk, as well as other basics you plan to pick up.

household-paperwork-2.solvingTip: Find the ink-writing tool at 2 Down. One crossing helps name the signed payment you put into the envelope at 3 Across.

clues.SEAL: Press the envelope flap down so it stays shut
clues.ENVELOPE: Paper holder used to mail a signed payment

notes.ENVELOPE: A bill can come with a return envelope for the payment. Its printed address shows where the signed check is meant to go.
notes.STAMP: A stamp pays postage on the bill's return envelope. Some reply envelopes already have a printed postage marking, so the front can show whether a stamp is needed.

household-paperwork-3.solvingTip: Try the short word for a single square on the calendar at 3 Across. It crosses the span of all twelve months at 4 Down.

notes.NUMBER: The number in a calendar square tells which date it is within that month. The column heading tells which day of the week it is.
notes.CALENDAR: A wall calendar lets you see dates for a whole month at once. A note in a square can put the time of an appointment next to its date.
notes.CIRCLE: Draw a circle around a date to pick it out among the other numbers. Keep the line outside the number so the date is easy to read at a glance.

clues.NUMBER: Mark in a calendar square showing the date within the month
clues.CALENDAR: Chart on the wall with a square for each date
clues.CIRCLE: Round line drawn around a date

household-paperwork-4.solvingTip: Start with the letters and envelopes that arrive together at 4 Across. Its crossing names where you spread them out to sort them at 1 Down.

notes.ENVELOPE: An unopened envelope can keep a bill and any inserts in one place until you are ready to sort them. The sender printed on the outside can help you decide which pile it belongs in.
notes.LETTER: A personal letter can be put aside to read after you sort the bills. Keeping it with its envelope can preserve the sender's return address.
notes.STAMP: A stamp can stick to the outside of an envelope among the morning mail. A postmark may run over it and show where or when the letter was handled.

clues.LETTER: Personal message on paper that may arrive with the morning mail

household-paperwork-5.solvingTip: Look for the little label that sticks up above a folder at 10 Across. It crosses the action of putting similar papers together at 8 Down.

notes.PAPER: Put each loose paper into a folder with the right subject. The tab at the top can still be read when the papers themselves are out of sight.
notes.LABEL: A few words on a folder label can describe a group of papers at a glance. Keep related labels together so it is easy to see where a new page belongs.

clues.PAPER: Sheet material you put into a file folder
clues.LABEL: Tag showing what kind of papers are in a folder

fresh-laundry.solvingTip: Try the short name for a fastener that holds a shirt up to dry at 12 Down. Its crossing helps you name the cord stretched between the poles at 11 Across.

clues.PIN: Fasten wet fabric to the line with a clip
clues.SHEET: Large piece of bedding that can hang from a clothesline
clues.SHIRT: Sleeved garment pegged on the line

notes.SHEET: A wet sheet can be hung with its corners spread along the line. Pegs keep the cloth in place while air can move along its surface.
notes.POLE: The pole holds the clothesline up off the grass. It keeps a long sheet from brushing the ground as the cloth hangs down to dry.
notes.SHIRT: Hang a wet shirt with space on either side. That gives the breeze room to reach the cloth instead of leaving it pressed against a sheet.

fresh-laundry-2.solvingTip: Begin with what you do when you bring the fabric edges together at 3 Down. A crossing leads to the cloth you put on the shelf at 4 Across.

clues.TOWEL: Absorbent cloth folded and put away after drying
clues.COTTON: Plant fiber often used in absorbent bath towels
clues.CORNER: Point where two edges of a towel meet

notes.SHELF: A shelf gives the folded towels a flat place to rest. Stacking them with the folds facing forward makes each towel easier to pick out.
notes.COTTON: Cotton loops help a bath towel take up water. After the towel is dry, folding the edges inward makes a neat stack on the shelf.
notes.CORNER: Match two corners of a towel before smoothing the fold across it. Lining up the corners keeps one layer from sticking out beyond the rest.

fresh-laundry-3.solvingTip: Find the garment that comes in a pair and goes inside a shoe at 2 Down. Its crossing helps name the container the clean laundry came out of at 6 Across.

clues.CUFF: Band at the top of a sock

notes.BASKET: A laundry basket can hold socks while you look for matches. Set a completed pair to one side so it stays together while you sort the rest.
notes.COTTON: Cotton is one fiber used to make socks. Since several pairs may be made from the same fiber, a stripe or a patterned cuff can help you find the match.
notes.DRAWER: A drawer can hold stacks or rows of paired socks. Put the ones still waiting for a match at one end so they are easy to find after the next wash.

fresh-laundry-4.solvingTip: Look for the heated tool that removes wrinkles at 7 Down. Its crossing names the action you take as you lower the tool onto the cloth at 9 Across.

clues.CORD: Covered wire that carries power from the outlet to the iron
clues.TABLE: Piece of furniture you can cover with a cloth before dinner
clues.CLOTH: Woven material spread over a table
clues.CREASE: Fold line in a tablecloth that ironing can flatten

notes.TABLE: The dining table is what the cloth will cover. Iron the cloth on an ironing board, then check how evenly it hangs over the table's edges.
notes.COTTON: A cotton tablecloth can crease along the lines where it was folded. Use the fabric setting that matches the care label when pressing those lines out.
notes.CLOTH: Here cloth means the fabric spread over the table. After pressing, you can smooth it out so the long edges fall evenly on both sides.

fresh-laundry-5.solvingTip: Start with what cleans the sweater in the basin at 3 Across. Then try the crossing for the part that covers an arm at 3 Down.

clues.SLEEVE: Part of a sweater covering an arm
clues.SINK: Basin where the sweater is soaked and rinsed
clues.WATER: Clear liquid that carries soap out of a rinsed sweater

notes.TOWEL: A towel laid flat can take up some of the moisture from a washed sweater. The basin is where the earlier soaking and rinsing happen.
notes.WATER: Rinsing a hand-washed sweater in fresh water carries away soap left in the fibers. A towel can take up extra moisture before you lay the sweater flat.

home-cleaning-corners.solvingTip: Think of the little vessel you drink from at 11 Down. It crosses the frame you set it on after rinsing at 10 Across.

clues.RACK: Frame where washed dishes are set to dry
clues.TOWEL: Cloth used to rub water off clean dishes

notes.WATER: The soapy water helps loosen food from a dish. Rinsing uses fresh water to carry off the soap before the dish goes onto the rack.
notes.PLATE: A plate can stand on its edge between two bars of the rack. That lets the rinse water run off instead of collecting on the surface.
notes.TOWEL: A drying towel can catch drops left on a washed dish. It can also take up the water that collects on the counter below the rack.

home-cleaning-corners-2.solvingTip: Try the fine dirt you wipe away at 6 Across. Its crossing names the flat place you lift the books from before wiping at 7 Down.

notes.SHELF: Dust can collect on the shelf under a frame or vase. Lifting one item at a time lets you wipe the area it was covering.
notes.FEATHER: Soft feathers can form the head of a duster. They can reach into the space behind the books or around the edges of a frame.
notes.CLOTH: A soft cloth can wipe a wider area of shelf than the tip of a duster. Folding it over gives you a fresh surface after one side collects dust.

clues.FEATHER: Light bird covering used to make some dusters

home-cleaning-corners-3.solvingTip: At 5 Across, find the thing you sweep the grit into. Use a crossing for the place where two edges of the steps meet at 2 Down.

clues.PAN: Shallow scoop you sweep dust and leaves into
clues.PORCH: Level entrance platform at the top of the front steps
clues.CORNER: Place where two sides of a step meet

notes.HANDLE: A long broom handle lets you reach the step below you. The bristles at the far end bend and pull loose leaves along the surface.
notes.PORCH: The porch floor is the level surface at the top of the steps. Loose leaves can be swept away from the corners before you work down the steps.
notes.CORNER: Dirt can collect in the corner where a step meets a side wall. The end of the broom can draw that debris out into the open.

home-cleaning-corners-4.solvingTip: Find the basin beneath the mirror at 4 Across. At 1 Down, its crossing asks what the mirror does when it reflects light after cleaning.

clues.FRAME: Rigid border holding the mirror glass
clues.SINK: Basin beneath the mirror where water drains away
clues.GLASS: Smooth clear surface you wipe on the front of a mirror
clues.MIRROR: Reflective surface you wipe above the sink
clues.SPRAY: Fine drops of cleaner on the mirror

notes.FRAME: The frame supports the glass at its edges. A separate mounting bracket may help hold the mirror against the wall.
notes.GLASS: The glass is the front surface you wipe. A layer behind it reflects the image, so a spot on the front can still interrupt what you see.
notes.MIRROR: Faint streaks on the mirror can be easier to see from the side. Turn your head a little after wiping to check where the spray has dried.

home-cleaning-corners-5.solvingTip: Try the piece of furniture you make up at 9 Across. Its crossing points to the large piece of cloth you tuck around the mattress at 8 Down.

notes.SHEET: A fitted sheet stretches around the corners of the mattress. A flat sheet lies above it and can be tucked along the bottom of the bed.
notes.BLANKET: The blanket goes on above the sheet. Straightening it across the bed gives it a similar amount of overhang on both sides.
notes.FOLD: Fold the top edge of the flat sheet down over the blanket. The folded edge leaves a strip of sheet where the bedding meets the pillows.

clues.FOLD: Turn the sheet's top edge down over the blanket

useful-home-repairs.solvingTip: Start with the round part you turn to open the door at 3 Across. It crosses the condition that makes the handle wobble at 2 Down.

clues.LATCH: Small fastening that keeps a door shut
clues.METAL: Hard material used to make screws and hinges

notes.HANDLE: The handle is what you hold to open the door. The nearby screw secures it, and the latch is the part that holds the door closed.
notes.METAL: The screw and the pieces it holds can be made of metal. The screw presses the handle's base against the door when it is tight.
notes.SCREW: The head of the loose screw is where the tip of the driver fits. Turning it seats the fastener more firmly so the handle can sit tight against the door.

useful-home-repairs-2.solvingTip: Look at 1 Down for the small metal fastener that goes into the wall. A crossing helps with the tool that strikes it at 3 Across.

notes.GLASS: The clear pane in the frame protects the picture. When you use a level to straighten the frame, rest it on the wooden edge.
notes.PENCIL: Use a pencil to make a small mark where the picture hook will go. A light mark can be erased if the place changes after measuring.

clues.PENCIL: Writing tool used to mark a spot for a picture hook

useful-home-repairs-3.solvingTip: Try the part that lights up inside the lamp at 6 Down. Its crossing names the part that rests on the table at 6 Across.

clues.SHADE: Cover around a lamp that softens its glare
clues.BULB: Part of a lamp that gives off light
clues.CLIP: Small fastener that holds the lamp covering in place
clues.TABLE: Piece of furniture that a small lamp rests on

notes.SHADE: The shade covers the brightest part of the lamp. It can spread the light or direct more of it toward the table.
notes.TABLE: A table lamp has a base that rests on a piece of furniture. Its shade fits higher up, around the bulb.
notes.LIGHT: The bulb gives off the light. A fabric shade can soften its glare and let more light fall through the openings at the top and bottom.

useful-home-repairs-4.solvingTip: Find the liquid that helps a squeaky hinge move smoothly at 6 Across. Then look for what you do to shut the cabinet at 4 Down.

clues.OIL: Slippery liquid used to quiet a squeaky hinge
clues.CLOTH: Piece of fabric used to wipe oil from a hinge
clues.METAL: Hard material the plates of a cabinet hinge can be made from
clues.DOOR: Movable panel that closes a cabinet

notes.CLOTH: A small cloth can catch a drop of oil under the hinge. You can use a clean corner of it to wipe off any oil left on the cabinet.
notes.METAL: The hinge can have two metal plates joined by a pin. The plates turn around that pin as the cabinet door opens and closes.

at-the-writing-desk.solvingTip: Find what you hold to make ink marks at 10 Across. Its crossing at 7 Down names the action of putting words on the page.

clues.WRITE: Put the words of a message on paper
clues.LETTER: Written message that can share news with a grandchild

notes.PAPER: Your note goes on the paper, and the address goes on the envelope. Leave room at the end of the last page for the closing and your name.
notes.ENVELOPE: Fold the pages of the letter together so they fit inside one envelope. If there are several pages, a page number helps your grandchild read them in order.
notes.LETTER: A letter to a grandchild can include a small piece of family news or a question for the next reply. Dating the first page gives the reader a time to remember it by.

at-the-writing-desk-2.solvingTip: Look at 1 Down for the three-letter word before code in a mailing address. A crossing helps with the other kind of number in the book at 4 Across.

clues.LETTER: One alphabet symbol used to group names in an address book
clues.ADDRESS: Street and postal details you might look up in a small book
clues.STREET: Road name written beside a building number in an address

notes.LETTER: An address book can have one section for each initial. Search under the first letter of a last name to find the entry.
notes.ADDRESS: An address book keeps a friend's street and postal details with their name. A phone number can go on a nearby line so both ways of reaching the person are easy to find.
notes.STREET: The street name in an address book belongs beside the building number. Together they help you find the right door on that road.

at-the-writing-desk-3.solvingTip: Begin with the everyday name for the pencil's dark center at 2 Across. Its crossing names the rubber piece used to remove a mark at 3 Down.

notes.PENCIL: Sharpening a wooden pencil exposes more of the writing core. A point with a little graphite showing can make small letters easier to fit inside a crossword square.
notes.RUBBER: A rubber eraser can lift the dark mark left by a pencil. When little bits of eraser collect on the puzzle, brush them away from the squares before writing again.
notes.ERASER: Use the eraser on just the square you want to change. A narrow corner of it lets you clear one letter while keeping the answers beside it readable.

clues.RUBBER: Flexible material that can be used in a pencil eraser
clues.ERASER: Tool used to rub out a wrong pencil answer

at-the-writing-desk-4.solvingTip: Try the small stack of sheets used for jottings at 9 Down. It crosses the compartment you pull open to reach the supplies at 11 Across.

clues.PAD: Small block of paper for jotting things down
clues.PIN: Short pointed fastener you press into a notice board
clues.DRAWER: Pull-out desk compartment that can hold clips and pens
clues.RUBBER: Flexible material used to make some erasers and bands

notes.DRAWER: The drawer keeps small supplies close to the desk surface. A shallow box inside it can keep clips and pins from mixing with the pens.
notes.RUBBER: Rubber bands and rubber erasers have different uses even when they share a drawer. A band stretches around a stack of papers, and an eraser can fix a pencil mark.
notes.ERASER: A separate eraser in the desk drawer can give you a wider edge than the one on a pencil. Keep it with the writing supplies so it is easy to reach during a small correction.

at-the-writing-desk-5.solvingTip: Look for the short message you are writing at 8 Down. At 10 Across, its crossing asks for what you sign at the bottom.

notes.PAPER: A folded sheet gives you an inside surface for the thank-you message. Naming the gift or the kind act makes the short note more personal.
notes.ENVELOPE: A small thank-you card can fit into an envelope without another fold. The flap closes over the card so its message stays private while it travels.
notes.THANKS: Many thanks is a familiar way to close a handwritten note. It can go on the line above your signature.

clues.PAPER: Sheet material you write a thank-you note on

through-the-front-door.solvingTip: Find the wet dirt you brush off before coming in at 9 Across. Its crossing helps you spell the name of the rug beside the threshold at 5 Down.

clues.MUD: Wet dirt you wipe off your boots at the door
clues.PORCH: Area just outside the front door where visitors can wipe their feet
clues.BRUSH: Bristled tool for cleaning dried mud from boots
clues.BOOT: Footwear you might wipe on a mat before coming inside

notes.PORCH: The porch gives visitors a place to stop before crossing the threshold. A mat there catches some of the dirt from their boots.
notes.BRUSH: A stiff brush can loosen dried mud from a boot before you use the doormat. Short bristles can reach the grooves in the sole.
notes.BOOT: Press the boot's sole against the coarse doormat before you step inside. Its fibers can catch loose grit from the raised parts of the tread.

through-the-front-door-2.solvingTip: Try the thin support that holds the umbrella open at 8 Across. Then look for what drips off when you bring it inside at 4 Down.

clues.WATER: Liquid dripping from the wet umbrella
clues.CLOTH: Fabric stretched over an umbrella's ribs

notes.WATER: A stand gives the dripping umbrella a place to rest. Some stands have a tray at the bottom to catch the drops.
notes.HANDLE: When you set an umbrella in a stand, the handle stays near the top. The wet fabric below can drip into the stand instead of onto the floor.
notes.CLOTH: The umbrella's cloth stretches over the ribs when it is open. Drops collect along the folds after it is shut and can run into the stand.

through-the-front-door-3.solvingTip: Start with the outer garment you take off indoors at 4 Down. Its crossing points to the curved piece on the wall at 5 Across.

clues.HOOK: Curved piece on the wall to hang an outdoor coat on

notes.HOOK: A hook bears the weight of a coat from its loop. A hanger holds the garment across both shoulders.

through-the-front-door-4.solvingTip: Look at 9 Across for the metal piece shaped to open the lock. A crossing helps with the word for the extra one set aside at 5 Down.

notes.HOUSE: A house key usually belongs to one of the building's doors. A spare hung in a familiar place can be found without sorting through a whole key ring.
notes.METAL: The key's metal keeps its small ridges and cuts from bending in everyday use. Those shapes help one key fit its lock.

clues.HOUSE: Building you unlock before coming home

through-the-front-door-5.solvingTip: Find what holds the cut flowers at 8 Down. One crossing leads to the piece of furniture it rests on at 10 Across.

notes.DRAWER: A small drawer in the entry table can hold spare items such as a key or a pen. The top of the table stays clear for the lamp and things you pick up daily.
notes.PHOTO: A photo on the entry table can show a person or place you recognize when you come in the door. A small stand behind its frame keeps the picture upright.
notes.MIRROR: An entry mirror lets you check a collar or hat before leaving. The small table below can hold what you need to pick up as you go out.

clues.MIRROR: Reflective glass that may hang over a small entry table

restful-household-routines.solvingTip: Begin with the control you turn to fill the tub at 2 Down. It shares a square with what makes a lather at 5 Across.

notes.TOWEL: Leave a towel near the tub so it is easy to reach when the bath ends. A separate mat can catch drops under your feet while you dry off.
notes.ROBE: A bathrobe can be put on after drying off with a towel. Its belt holds the loose front closed while you move away from the tub.

restful-household-routines-2.solvingTip: Try the word for opening your mouth when sleepy at 1 Down. Its crossing names the dark hours when you go to sleep at 5 Across.

notes.NIGHT: Here night is the part of the day set aside for winding down. The bedside book and pillow are part of that routine.
notes.SHEET: The sheet is the light layer on the bed just below a blanket. Pulling that layer smooth can make it easier to slide into bed.
notes.CLOCK: A clock beside the bed lets you check the time after the evening's reading. An alarm on the same clock can be set before you put the book down.

clues.CLOCK: Bedside device that shows the time

restful-household-routines-3.solvingTip: Look for the place you lie down to sleep at 9 Across. A crossing leads to the piece of furniture beside it at 6 Down.

notes.WATER: The water in this scene is the drink beside the bed. A glass on the table is easy to reach for a sip without getting up.
notes.GLASS: The glass is the vessel on the bedside table. Clear sides let you see how much water is left without picking it up.
notes.DRAWER: A nightstand drawer keeps small belongings below the tabletop. That leaves the glass of water and the book within reach above it.

clues.WATER: Clear drink in the glass beside the bed
clues.GLASS: Small drinking vessel on the nightstand
clues.DRAWER: Pull-out compartment in a bedside table
clues.CLOCK: Timepiece that sits beside the bed

restful-household-routines-5.solvingTip: Find the drawing that shows the roads at 9 Down. Its crossing names the drink you pack in a bottle at 10 Across.

clues.WATER: Clear drink carried in a bottle on a day out

notes.WATER: Water travels in a bottle in the day bag. Closing the bottle securely helps keep stray drops away from the tissues and map.
notes.HANDLE: A day bag's handle is the part you lift it by. A pocket keeps small items within reach, and the zipper closes the opening.

on-the-local-road.solvingTip: Try the action of coming to a halt at 4 Down. It crosses the part of the signal that shows when to do it at 5 Across.

clues.LIGHT: Signal that changes color to tell cars when to stop

notes.BUTTON: The button on a pole sends a request for the pedestrian signal. Look for the walk symbol before stepping off the curb.

on-the-local-road-2.solvingTip: Look at 8 Across for what goes in the parking space. Its crossing names the device that tracks the paid time at 6 Down.

clues.TICKET: Printed slip showing payment or a parking violation
clues.METER: Device beside a parking space that records paid time
clues.SLOT: Narrow opening in a meter where a coin goes
clues.STREET: Town road with marked parking spaces at the curb

notes.TICKET: A parking ticket is tied to a parked car or parking space. It can record payment or show that a parking rule was broken.
notes.STREET: The street has a curb where the car can pull into a marked space. The meter measures parking time for that space beside the square.

on-the-local-road-3.solvingTip: Find the everyday three-letter name for the fuel at 3 Across. Its crossing points to the flexible tube between the pump and the nozzle at 1 Down.

clues.HOSE: Flexible tube carrying fuel from the pump to the car
